summary.short: SB 21-190 (Colorado Privacy Act) gives Colorado consumers rights over their personal data and imposes duties on controllers and processors that do business in Colorado or target residents, enforced by the Attorney General and district attorneys, from July 1, 2023.
summary.long: SB 21-190 enacts the Colorado Privacy Act as Part 13 of Article 1 of Title 6, effective July 1, 2023. It covers controllers that conduct business in Colorado or target products to Colorado residents and process personal data of 100,000 or more consumers a year, or 25,000 or more while deriving revenue from selling data. Exemptions include HIPAA-covered health information, Gramm-Leach-Bliley financial institutions, FCRA-regulated activity and employment records. Consumers may access, correct, delete, port and opt out of targeted advertising, data sales and certain profiling; controllers must respond within 45 days, provide appeals, and honor universal opt-out mechanisms meeting Attorney General specifications from July 1, 2024. Controllers must give privacy notices, specify purposes, minimize data, avoid secondary use without consent, secure data, avoid unlawful discrimination, and obtain consent before processing sensitive data, including a known child's data with parental consent. Processing that presents a heightened risk of harm requires documented data protection assessments, available to the Attorney General on request. Processors must follow controller instructions under binding contracts. The Attorney General and district attorneys enforce the Act, with no private right of action; violations are deceptive trade practices, and penalty amounts are not stated here.
